Keep Silent Bands Off the Bottom

The five bars cover bass to treble from left to right. Each bar follows its own band: it grows when the band is louder than its recent average and shrinks when it is quieter. Changes apply immediately, so you can compare while music plays.
Higher values make the bars move more gently but follow the beat a little later. At 0 there is no smoothing: most responsive, and most jittery.

How much recent music is used to judge whether the current moment is loud or quiet. Shorter values make every beat stand out; longer values bring out the contrast between longer sections such as verse and chorus.
Higher values need a bigger swing to reach full height, so the bars move less overall. Lower values let small changes reach the top.
After a bar turns from growing to shrinking (or back), it stays at least this long before turning again. Raise it to reduce back-and-forth jitter; 0 means no hold.
How far a bar moves toward its target each frame. Higher is snappier, lower is softer. Rise and fall are set separately, for example a fast rise with a slow fall.

When on, a band that briefly goes silent is treated as very quiet and its bar shrinks gradually; when off, the bar drops to its shortest at once. When every band is silent, all five bars drop to their shortest.

HyperIsland touch controls apply only to the music island and do not affect other HyperIsland content. The camera splits the HyperIsland into a left area and a right area, each with its own actions; with “Use the Same Settings on Both Sides” on, both areas share one set. An expanded HyperIsland keeps system controls.
Directions without an action stay with the system; once assigned, a swipe in that direction runs only the chosen action, however far it goes.
With double tap on, a single tap waits one double-tap interval before it runs; with it off, rapid taps all count as single taps.
Seeking needs player support, continuous volume works only with left and right swipes, and mute affects local media audio only.
